name: Sum of Multiples of 3 or 5 below n
description: Adds every number below n divisible by 3 or 5, by inclusion–exclusion with arithmetic-series sums (Project Euler problem 1).

name: Count of Multiples of a or b up to n
expression: floor(n / a) + floor(n / b) - floor(n / lcm(a, b))
description: Counts the numbers from 1 to n divisible by a or b (inclusion–exclusion), e.g. how many "Fizz", "Buzz" or "FizzBuzz" lines a FizzBuzz program prints.

name: Sum of Multiples of k up to n
description: Adds k + 2k + 3k + … up to n, using the triangular-number formula.
notes: The multiples of 7 up to 100 add up to 735.

name: Sum of Even Fibonacci Numbers up to x
description: Adds the even Fibonacci numbers not exceeding x (Project Euler problem 2). Every third Fibonacci number is even.
notes: Up to four million the sum is 4,613,732.

name: Square of Sum minus Sum of Squares
Sum of Digits of 1 … n
description: Adds the digit sums of all integers from 1 to n.
notes: From 1 to 100 the digits add up to 901.

name: Product of Digits
description: Multiplies the decimal digits of n.
notes: 39 → 27 → 14 → 4: repeating it gives the multiplicative persistence (3 steps for 39).

name: Kaprekar Routine Step (Four Digits)
expression: sum(k, 1, 4, at(sort(list(mod(floor(n / 1000), 10), mod(floor(n / 100), 10), mod(floor(n / 10), 10), mod(n, 10))), k) * 10^(k - 1)) - sum(k, 1, 4, at(sort(list(mod(floor(n / 1000), 10), mod(floor(n / 100), 10), mod(floor(n / 10), 10), mod(n, 10))), k) * 10^(4 - k))
description: Arranges the four digits of n in descending and ascending order and subtracts. Repeating this reaches 6174 (Kaprekar's constant) within 7 steps, unless all digits are equal.

name: Palindrome in Base b Test
expression: sum(k, 0, floor(logb(n, b) + 1e-9), mod(floor(n / b^k), b) * b^(floor(logb(n, b) + 1e-9) - k)) == n
description: Returns 1 when the base-b digits of n read the same in both directions.
notes: 585 is a palindrome both in decimal and in binary (1001001001).

name: Liouville's Constant (Partial Sum)
description: Adds 10^(−k!) for k = 1 … n; the infinite sum 0.110001000… is Liouville's constant, the first number proved transcendental (1844).
notes: Three terms give 0.110001; the next 1 appears at the 24th decimal place.

name: Area of a Pythagorean Triangle (Euclid)
description: Gives the area of the right triangle with legs m² − n² and 2mn from Euclid's formula.
notes: m = 5, n = 2 gives the (21, 20, 29) triangle with area 210. Such areas are always multiples of 6.

name: Perimeter of a Pythagorean Triangle (Euclid)
description: Gives the perimeter a + b + c = 2m(m + n) of the triangle from Euclid's formula.

name: Inradius of a Pythagorean Triangle (Euclid)
description: Gives the radius of the inscribed circle, (a + b − c)/2 = n(m − n), always a whole number.
